questions.q: In the full modern architecture, what typically connects the front-end to the database?
choices: A direct file link, with no server involved
An API on a server, usually returning JSON
questions.explanation: Letting a browser connect directly to a database would expose credentials and bypass all authorization logic. Instead, the browser talks to an API server, which validates the request, queries the database, and returns JSON — keeping credentials and business rules safely server-side.

questions.q: What is the key difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
choices: They are three names for the same thing
How much of the stack you rent versus build yourself
questions.explanation: IaaS (e.g., bare EC2 instances) gives you raw servers to configure however you like. PaaS (e.g., Heroku, Railway) manages the server layer so you just deploy code. SaaS (e.g., Supabase, Stripe) manages everything and you just call an API. Each step trades control for convenience.

questions.q: What is identified as the most valuable next step after this course?
choices: Building something real, however small, and documenting it clearly
Avoiding hosting anything until it's perfect
Skipping projects and going straight to interviews
questions.explanation: Every framework you could memorize will look different in two years. Building a real project forces you to make decisions, hit real problems, and develop the debugging instinct that's harder to teach than any specific technology.
